the lens took the light of one electric bulb and bent it into a white flash that went out over the water every ten seconds, all night, every night,
  in fair weather and foul.

  The lens did not forgive carelessness. Salt film crept over the glass if he let it, and dust found its way up seventy-four steps no matter how the
  door was kept, so every morning he went up with a linen cloth and wiped the prisms, and once a week he polished the brass rails until they held his
  face, warped and orange. The rest of the work was watching and writing it down. Wind, sea, visibility, passing vessels, anything out of the
  ordinary. Most entries were the same as the entries before them. The sameness was the work. Anyone who thought otherwise had never done it.

  He had not always lived alone. Irene came to the point as his wife in the spring of 1938 and stayed thirty minutes longer than any visitor had
  managed before her, and after that she stayed the rest of her life. She was a schoolteacher from the valley and she had never seen the ocean until
  she saw it from the tower stairs, and she said afterward that she had made up her mind on the forty-first step, the one that creaked. She hauled
  soil up from the beach in buckets and grew potatoes and peas in a garden the wind tried to take every year. She painted the kitchen yellow. She read
  aloud in the evenings while he mended the wiring, novels and newspaper serials and once, all the way through, the Almanac, which he had liked better
  than he let on.

  In their second winter a lumber schooner went on the rocks four miles north in a fog so thick the crew never saw the headlands, only the light,
  which they had been steering for since dusk without knowing it was there. Eleven men came ashore in a lifeboat and walked down the beach to the
  station at dawn, and Irene fed them everything in the house, and one of them, a Swede with a broken wrist, cried at the table and was not ashamed of
  it. Walter never forgot that. It was not that he had saved them, exactly. It was that the light had saved them and he had kept the light, and the
  difference was the whole shape of the job, and he explained this to nobody because nobody ever asked.
